title: Wren and the Summer
premise: Rafael Dravenmoor built his wedding-planning empire on the ruins of his own broken engagement, training himself to orchestrate other people's love while feeling none of it. When a charity pen-pal program accidentally pairs him—under a pseudonym—with Wren Calloway, the investigative journalist whose exposé nearly destroyed his company and whom he blames for his brother's ruin, their anonymous letters become the only place either tells the truth. As Rafael discovers Wren's exposé was suppressed by the same powerful family who once destroyed him, he must decide whether to protect his career by staying silent or hand her the evidence that will burn down both their enemies and his own carefully contained heart. In the end, Rafael testifies publicly, loses the business but wins back his integrity, and chooses Wren—not at a wedding he planned, but at a courthouse steps ceremony where memory, justice, and love finally align.
about_author: J. M. Underhill is a former event coordinator turned novelist who spent a decade watching love from behind the scenes before writing about it up close. Underhill lives in a coastal town where the fog rolls in like an unfinished sentence, and writes stories about people who mistake control for safety.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He directs a flawless society wedding with surgical detachment, narrating his philosophy that the heart is trainable muscle. A panic attack in the service corridor reveals the cost of containment. Emotional beat: polished surface over buried grief.

chapters.title: Anonymous Correspondents
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A burned-out journalist signs up for a library charity pen-pal program seeking honesty without bylines. She writes her first letter venting about power and impunity. Emotional beat: cautious hope that anonymity might restore her voice.

chapters.title: A Clerical Error
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The program's volunteer coordinator mismatches two entries; Rafael's letter reaches Wren, hers reaches him. Each recognizes something sharp and familiar in the stranger's words. Emotional beat: irritation curdling into reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: Enemies, Unnamed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a press gala she clashes publicly with Rafael Dravenmoor, unaware he is her pen pal 'Theo.' He deflects her questions about the Voss family's suppressed scandal. Emotional beat: antagonism sharpened by unacknowledged attraction.

chapters.title: Letters Without Faces
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Writing as Theo, he confesses doubts he'd never voice aloud, including guilt over his brother Daniel's bankruptcy after Wren's story ran. He begins investigating what really happened. Emotional beat: the first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Digging into old notes, Wren finds her Voss exposé was killed not for weak sourcing but by legal intimidation—and that Daniel Dravenmoor was a source she never knew. Emotional beat: guilt rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: The Gilded Client
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Marcus Voss hires Rafael to plan his daughter's wedding—the same family that ruined Daniel. Refusing means losing everything; accepting means proximity to proof. Emotional beat: ambition wrestling with dread.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Envelope
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Pen-pal letters deepen: Theo admits complicity in something unnamed; Wren admits she destroyed a man once. They almost recognize each other through shared wounds. Emotional beat: intimacy built on mutual confession.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner Reconnaissance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Covering the Voss wedding for a lifestyle piece, Wren overhears Marcus threatening Rafael about 'the Daniel problem.' She starts connecting threads between her pen pal's confessions and the case. Emotional beat: suspicion and sympathy colliding.

chapters.title: The Memory of Rain
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A rainstorm strands Rafael and Wren together post-site-visit; memories of his engagement surface, and they talk honestly for the first time off the page. Emotional beat: warmth neither can file away as professional.

chapters.title: Signed, Theo
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A phrase from Theo's letter echoes in Rafael's speech at the wedding tasting. Wren suspects the impossible and sets a trap—a fabricated detail only Theo would correct. Emotional beat: vertigo of realization.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael corrects the planted detail in his next letter and realizes mid-sentence what he's done. He must decide whether to confess his identity or vanish from the correspondence. Emotional beat: terror of being truly seen.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren confronts Rafael; fury and betrayal explode—she was his enemy experiment, he was her source's brother. Both say unforgivable things. Emotional beat: heartbreak as exposure, armor stripped raw.

chapters.title: Silence as Strategy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren throws herself into rebuilding the Voss investigation, but every lead now runs through Rafael. Meanwhile Marcus's lawyers circle her editor. Emotional beat: loneliness weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Daniel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Going through Daniel's stored boxes, Rafael finds a ledger documenting Voss fraud—evidence Daniel collected before his collapse. Rafael understands his brother wasn't broken by Wren's story but silenced by the Vosses. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into fury.

chapters.title: The Price of the Contract
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Marcus offers Rafael partnership and the deed to Daniel's old home in exchange for the ledger and continued silence. Rafael stalls, buying time, knowing refusal ends his career. Emotional beat: temptation measured against conscience.

chapters.title: An Open Letter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren publishes a piece on the pen-pal program's power to tell truths anonymously—her public signal to Theo that she forgives the deception and still believes in what they wrote. Emotional beat: an olive branch disguised as journalism.

chapters.title: The Wedding Day Gambit
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the Voss wedding itself, Rafael plans to slip the ledger to Wren during the reception chaos. Marcus anticipates him; security detains Rafael as Wren watches, understanding too late what he's sacrificing. Emotional beat: climax—love made visible through ruin.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael gives the ledger to federal investigators and testifies publicly, dismantling his own career and name. Flashbacks to Daniel frame his choice as belated justice outside any contract. Emotional beat: liberation through loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Voss empire falls; Wren's restored story runs front-page. She searches the wreckage for Rafael and finds his office emptied, one unsent letter addressed to her on the desk. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren finds Rafael at Daniel's reclaimed house. They read each other's final letters aloud—no pseudonyms, no containment. Forgiveness arrives not as absolution but as choice. Emotional beat: reconciliation earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Summer, Unplanned
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Months later, on the courthouse steps after the Voss verdicts, Rafael and Wren marry simply—no planner, no production, just witnesses and sunlight. Rafael finally believes the heart isn't containable after all. Emotional beat: quiet joy; memory honored, power undone, love chosen freely.
